broker.name: FOREX.com
broker.tagline: StoneX's retail forex brand. Protections, leverage and the minimum deposit depend on which group company you join.
broker.about: FOREX.com is a retail trading brand of StoneX Group, a Nasdaq-listed US company. The brand's base is Warren, New Jersey. It offers forex and, depending on the entity, CFDs on indices, commodities and shares, plus crypto. You are placed with a StoneX or GAIN company based on where you live, so the regulator and the rules are not the same for every client. RAW pricing advertises spreads from 0.0 pips plus a commission. Trading is on FOREX.com's web and mobile platforms, TradingView and MetaTrader 5.
broker.regulators_note: FOREX.com's international regulation page lists these authorities, including the US, Canada and the UK. Company names are filled in only where a customer agreement or the broker's own page names them. CIMA, MAS and the Japan FSA are listed by the broker without a company name. A Capital Markets Authority is also named on that page without a country or company, so it is left off this list.

plans.name: RAW pricing
plans.billing_note: Spreads from 0.0 pips on FX majors, plus a commission. US pages state $7 per $100,000 traded. The international RAW Spread page states $5 per $100,000 traded.

plans.name: Spread only
plans.billing_note: No separate commission. The cost sits in the spread. FOREX.com does not publish one typical pip figure for this account.

rows.label: RAW, United States
rows.note: $7 per $100,000 traded, charged on the open and again on the close. FOREX.com says spreads can widen when markets are fast or quiet.

rows.label: RAW, international
rows.note: $5 per $100,000 traded on the international RAW Spread account. The Cayman Islands page ties that account to CIMA oversight.

rows.label: Spread only
rows.note: FOREX.com does not publish one standard spread for this account. The live quote moves.

broker.costs_note: No single minimum is shown, because it depends on the company you join. US and international account pages say you can deposit from $100, and they recommend at least $2,500. That $100 figure may not apply everywhere.

leverage.note: FOREX.com does not publish one maximum for every client. US retail forex on major pairs is capped by the CFTC, commonly at 50:1. UK and EU retail clients are under a lower cap, commonly 30:1 on majors.

broker.leverage_note: Leverage increases losses as well as gains, and you can lose more than you deposit. The limit is set by the FOREX.com company you join and by the product.

other_fees.label: Minimum deposit
other_fees.note: US and international account pages say you can deposit from $100. That figure may not apply everywhere.

broker.promotions: A welcome bonus of up to $5,000, a switch offer of up to $10,000, referral rewards and Active Trader rebates have been advertised. Eligibility and amounts depend on the entity and the campaign.

MetaTrader 5 is added because the RAW account pages name it. Dollar amounts on the welcome bonus and switch offer were not re-opened on a promo page during this pass.
